terms.comment: lēgerō, I shall have read (Traupman 226). This is a modern category. The ancient grammarians count five tenses and do not make this one of them: Donatus puts lēgerō in the subjunctive, as its future (eōdem modō tempore futūrō cum lēgerō lēgeris lēgerit, Donatus, Ars minor, Dē verbō), and Priscian treats it likewise. We have not found who first said futūrum perfectum or futūrum exāctum. The plain future is futūrum, tempus futūrum (Traupman 226, 246).
The other usual name in modern grammars, “the completed future”.

sources: Lewis & Short: sum · Lewis & Short: perficio
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 226, 246.
